industry: Retail stores and grand openings (general retail, furniture, pharmacy, liquor, grocery, specialty)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Was $X' / 'compare at' / '% off' without a real former price offered in good faith for a reasonable period (16 CFR 233.1; state rules like CA B&P 17501)
'Up to X% off' if few items get X%
'While supplies last' without reasonable stock; 'first [N]' when the number isn't honored
'Same as cash', '0% interest', '$X/month' without Reg Z disclosures (12 CFR 1026.24 trigger terms) (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-049/063/064)
Raffles/drawings that require a purchase (illegal lottery risk); missing 'no purchase necessary' on mailed sweepstakes (39 USC 3001(k)) (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-034/053)
Prescription-transfer incentives (gift cards, coupons) for pharmacy grand openings without checking state pharmacy law and federal program rules (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-059)
Alcohol price/coupon promotions without state liquor rules (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-047)
Gift cards/'$X free card' without Reg E promotional labeling
compliance_notes: Former price comparisons (16 CFR 233, verified): the former price must be the actual price at which the item was openly and actively offered for a reasonable time in the recent past; 'compare at' must reflect real prices in the trade area.

Sweepstakes by mail (39 USC 3001(k), verified): must clearly and conspicuously state 'no purchase is necessary' and that 'a purchase will not improve an individual's chances of winning', in the mailing, in the rules and on the entry form, more conspicuously than other text; plus official rules, odds, prize values and sponsor. Purchase-required drawings can be illegal lotteries under state law.

Credit ads (Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24): trigger terms (down payment, number of payments, payment amount, finance charge) require full disclosures; 'deferred interest' needs specific wording. Use 'Financing available' if terms aren't ready.
Gift cards (Reg E 12 CFR 1005.20, verified): 5-year minimum; promotional cards must say 'promotional' on the front and show expiry and fees.

Pharmacy openings: inducements to Medicare/Medicaid beneficiaries are limited (OIG nominal value $15/item, $75/yr; no cash equivalents); many states restrict prescription-transfer incentives (not verified per state).
Alcohol retail promos: state rules vary (coupons, free items, price advertising); check each state.
'Limited quantities' must be honest; advertised items must be available in reasonable quantities or limits disclosed (FTC s.5; many state UDAP rules; not verified per state).
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, relief are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold-set raffles and drawings tied to purchase (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-034/053) vs 39 USC 3001(k) and state lottery law
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no-purchase-necessary entry with full disclosures, or drop the drawing.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Pharmacy prescription-transfer gift cards (GOLD-retail-grand-openings-059) vs OIG inducement rules and state pharmacy rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no transfer incentives to beneficiaries beyond nominal value; flag for counsel.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Discount-heavy retail encoding vs premium restraint (C-3PO)
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Not a legal conflict; match positioning. Discount encoding is a valid default in mass retail.
